## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The town and the hundred years  (`#the-town-and-the-hundred-years`)

Cited ayat: 2:259

> **2:259** أَوْ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحْىِۦ هَٰذِهِ ٱللَّهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِا۟ئَةَ عَامٍ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُۥ قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتَ قَالَ لَبِثْتُ يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ قَالَ بَل لَّبِثْتَ مِا۟ئَةَ عَامٍ فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ ءَايَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكْسُوهَا لَحْمًا فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥ قَالَ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

### Claims

**c1** (2:259): The Quran gives the case of one who passed by a town that had fallen in ruins over its roofs, and he asked how God would give it life after its death.

**c2** (2:259): God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him.

**c3** (2:259): He was asked how long he had stayed, and he said a day or part of a day, and he was told that he had stayed a hundred years.

**c4** (2:259): He was told to look at his food and drink, which had not spoiled, and at his donkey, so that God might make him a sign for the people, and to look at the bones, how God sets them together and then clothes them with flesh.

**c5** (2:259): When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things.

### One-minute summary

A man passed by a town that had fallen in ruins and asked how God would give it life after its death [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].

### Complete story

The Quran gives the case of one who passed by a town that had fallen in ruins over its roofs, and he asked how God would give it life after its death [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. He was asked how long he had stayed, and he said a day or part of a day, and he was told that he had stayed a hundred years [c3]. He was told to look at his food and drink, which had not spoiled, and at his donkey, so that God might make him a sign for the people, and to look at the bones, how God sets them together and then clothes them with flesh [c4]. When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].

### Deep study

The ayah does not name the man or the town [c1]. It does not say who asked him how long he had stayed [c3]. The Arabic for how God sets the bones together is read in more than one way in the recitations [c4].

### Kids mode

A man passed by a town that had fallen in ruins [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. He thought he had stayed a day or part of a day, and was told that it was a hundred years [c3]. He said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the man's question about the town is answered by what happened to him [c1][c2]. Another is that his last words are a statement that God has power over all things [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the man's name, his faith or whether he was a prophet; the ayah calls him one who passed by a town.
- Not established: the name of the town, or who destroyed it.
- Not established: who asked him how long he had stayed; the ayah does not name the speaker.
- Not established: what the sign for the people was, beyond the words of the ayah.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man and the town are identified in later works.
